question: Should Control UI adopt `/new --name <title>` as a supported named-session creation grammar while all other `/new <text>` forms and non-Control-UI surfaces keep their existing semantics?
rationale: Code review can establish correctness, but only maintainers can accept a new public command contract and its deliberate cross-surface asymmetry.

options.title: Close pending sponsorship
options.body: Keep the existing `/new` then `/name` workflow and reopen this technically ready branch if a maintainer sponsors the new grammar.

options.title: Accept the narrow option
options.body: Sponsor `/new --name <title>` for Control UI only and preserve every existing bare, arbitrary-text, and non-Control-UI `/new` behavior.

options.title: Design shared semantics
options.body: Pause this branch and define one named-session creation grammar in the shared command layer before adding a Control UI shortcut.

recommendation.title: Close pending sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep the existing `/new` then `/name` workflow and reopen this technically ready branch if a maintainer sponsors the new grammar.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice changes a documented user-facing Control UI command, and repository context plus the contributor's explicit review request point here as the best available decision owner.
